# iliad-107 — renderings chosen for 16.777–867 (to be copied into conventions.md)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| τερμιόεσσα (ἀσπίς, 16.803; sense not known) | "with a border" | "bordered" (+ note: from τέρμα "end, edge"; sense not certain) | "tasselled", "fringed", "rimmed"; follows the Odyssey table’s τερμιόεις (19.242) |
| ἦμαρ ἀναγκαῖον (16.836; against ἐλεύθερον ἦμαρ 16.831) | "the day of necessity" | "the day of necessity" | "the day of slavery", "of compulsion"; keeps the pair with the table's ἐλεύθερον ἦμαρ "day of freedom" (6.455) |
| μεταπρέπω (16.835) | "am conspicuous" | "am conspicuous among" | "stand out" (the Odyssey’s `i`, but the Iliad’s own rows 2.481, 11.720 and 16.596 have "conspicuous" in `i`), "excel", "am pre-eminent" |
| ἡλικίην ἐκέκαστο (16.808) | "excelled those of his age" | "excelled men of his age" | "surpassed" (reserved for νικάω), "outdid his peers"; ἐκέκαστο keeps "excelled" (2.530, iliad-027) |
| ὀρωρέχαται (16.834) | "are stretched out" | "are straining forward" | "reach", "are eager" |
| ἐξεναρίζεις (16.850, the killing already told) | "are despoiling" | "are stripping me of my armour" | "kill and strip" (the table’s row where the killing is in the verb); follows 6.417 (`l` "despoil", `i` "strip of his armour") |
| ἵετο γὰρ βαλέειν · τὸν δ’ ἔκφερον ὠκέες ἵπποι (16.866, with ἄμβροτοι … ἀγλαὰ δῶρα 16.867) | "for he was eager to strike;" · "but him the swift horses bore out, deathless, which to Peleus the gods gave, splendid gifts." | "for he longed to strike him;" · "the swift, deathless horses, which the gods gave to Peleus as splendid gifts, were carrying Automedon out." | the published iliad-102 `i` names Hector as the one carried off; here τὸν is Automedon, so the pronoun is named differently and the rest keeps the published wording |
